## About

I am a physician from Ghana with a strong interest in chronic disease epidemiology, particularly cardiovascular and cardiometabolic conditions. My long-term goal is to design and lead clinical trials focused on non-communicable diseases in Sub-Saharan Africa, especially in Ghana. I want to gain as much practical research experience and quantitative skills, particularly in the design and implementation of clinical trials, and to understand how such trials shape public health interventions and policies.

I have worked as a clinician since graduating from medical school, with my most recent role as a Medical Officer in the Department of Anesthesia at the [Korle Bu Teaching Hospital](https://kbth.gov.gh/), Ghana’s largest tertiary referral center.

Currently, I am an MPH candidate in the Epidemiology/Biostatistics concentration at the [Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health](https://publichealth.jhu.edu/)

##### Interests

-   Clinical Trials and Research
-   Chronic Disease Epidemiology
-   Data Analysis

#### Side Note

Project Zero seemed very daunting, but working on it has been very fun and enlightening. The instructions were quite clear and informative. I had no programming experience coming into the MPH program and I wanted to gain at least an intermediary level of skill in R-programming so I could write codes without having to rely on ChatGPT. Hopefully by week 8 of this course I should be halfway there in writing codes in R and understanding R Syntax.
Grateful to God for the opportunity. And I am glad my friend, [Kwabena Asabere](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kwabenaasabere), recommended this course to me.
